## Overview

My research examines how people, relationships, and innovation activity are organised across institutions, cities, and regions. The current agenda develops through three connected directions: high-skilled mobility and location choice, scientific collaboration networks and relational dynamics, and corporate innovation and knowledge assets, with cities and regional innovation serving as the shared spatial and institutional context.

:::

::: {.page-band .surface}

## High-Skilled Mobility & Location Choice

This stream studies the movement of high-skilled scientific talent across cities and institutions, with attention to mobility networks, career stages, destination alternatives, and the city-level conditions that structure observed moves.

::: {.stream-output-grid}
::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-accepted">Accepted · First Author</span></p>
<h3>Spatial Structure and Determinants of Global Top Biomedical Scientists' Mobility from an Urban Network Perspective</h3>
<p>Analyzes the intercity mobility network of global top biomedical scientists, career-stage differences, and city-level factors associated with mobility ties.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> 500 scientists; 1970-2023 career histories; 398 cities; 1,440 intercity mobility links; learning- and work-stage mobility records; city science and innovation attributes.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> career-history reconstruction; directed weighted intercity mobility network; social network analysis; GIS spatial analysis; Heckman two-step model.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#high-skilled-mobility){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted · First Author</span></p>
<h3>Structure and Formation Mechanisms of Intercity Mobility Networks of Global Top Biomedical Scientists: A Whole-Network and Ego-Network Perspective</h3>
<p>Extends the mobility agenda by combining whole-network structure with ego-network measures and career-trajectory information.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> long-term career histories for a top-scientist roster; city-level mobility networks; ego-network subsample; collaboration and career-stage information.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> whole-network analysis; ego-network analysis; constraint; effective size; Shannon entropy; weighted ERGM; GIS.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#whole-ego-mobility){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted · First Author</span></p>
<h3>Pre-move coauthor ties and the direction of scientific mobility: A city-level choice analysis of highly cited biomedical scientists</h3>
<p>Examines whether direct coauthor ties before a move distinguish selected destination cities from candidate alternatives among highly cited biomedical scientists.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> observed mobility events; focal scientists; candidate-city choice sets; pre-move coauthor ties; city-level destination alternatives.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> event-specific candidate-set construction; conditional logit; pre-move tie measurement; geographic-distance control; robustness and timing checks.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#pre-move-coauthor-ties){.publication-link}
:::
:::

## Scientific Collaboration Networks & Relational Dynamics

This stream studies scientific collaboration as a longitudinal relational process. The current manuscript follows dormant coauthor relations and observes whether joint publication recurs after a complete publication hiatus.

::: {.stream-output-grid}
::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-submitted">Submitted · First Author</span></p>
<h3>When Coauthorship Goes Quiet: Relational History, Portfolio Context, and the Recurrence of Scientific Ties</h3>
<p>Studies how prior relationship history, current collaboration-portfolio breadth, and elapsed dormancy are associated with observed coauthorship recurrence after publication dormancy.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> longitudinal focal-scientist publication records; recurrent focal-scientist-prior-coauthor dormant spells; annual risk-year observations; primary publication-hiatus definition.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> recurrent dormant-spell construction; discrete-time event-history analysis; complementary-log-log model; clustered covariance; standardized adjusted predictions; threshold and measurement robustness analyses.</p>
<p><strong>Interpretation boundary:</strong> coauthorship recurrence is an observable bibliometric event, not evidence of intentional reconnection, restored trust, or resumed interpersonal contact.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#after-collaboration-goes-quiet){.publication-link}
:::
:::

:::

## Corporate Innovation & Knowledge Assets

This stream builds a measurement foundation for comparing firm-level technological and brand-oriented innovation within the same empirical structure.

::: {.stream-output-grid}
::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-output">Data System in Progress</span></p>
<h3>Firm-Year Innovation Data System</h3>
<p>This project builds firm-year data for leading global R&D firms by linking R&D expenditure, patents, trademarks, industry, country, firm identity, and year, so technology-oriented and market-oriented innovation can be analyzed in a shared empirical structure.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> high-R&D firms; patents; trademarks; industry and country fields.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> entity matching; intellectual-property linkage; panel construction; measurement audit.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#corporate-innovation){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<p><span class="status-badge status-output">Research Design and Data Construction in Progress</span></p>
<h3>Technology-Brand Innovation Portfolios</h3>
<p>This direction compares how patent portfolios and trademark portfolios co-appear within firms, without reducing innovation to a single output count.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> linked intellectual-property records; firm-year observations.</p>
<p><strong>Methods:</strong> indicator construction; portfolio comparison; type description.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#corporate-innovation){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item .research-project-card}
<h3>Dynamic Evolution and Spatial Context</h3>
<p>The firm-year panel also supports analysis of temporal change. The current design focuses on how innovation portfolios vary by industry, country, firm characteristics, and regional innovation environment.</p>
<p><strong>Data:</strong> annual firm innovation records; industry and country context.</p>
[View Output →](publications.html#corporate-innovation){.publication-link}
:::
:::

:::
